\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بے} \ur{ہوش} (be hosh)}{بے ہوش (be hosh)}]{\ur{بے} \ur{ہوش} (be hosh) — unconscious}

\label{lesson:UR-C286-be-hosh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to be grazed, then the Urdu for a scratch.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بے} \ur{ہوش}}
\textbf{\ur{بے} \ur{ہوش}} — \emph{be hosh} — \textquotedblleft{}unconscious\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{وہ} \ur{آدمی} \ur{بے} \ur{ہوش} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{voh ādmī be hosh thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
That man was unconscious.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بے} \ur{ہوش}} (\emph{be hosh}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{bē-hōsh}, built from \emph{bē}, \textquotedblleft{}without\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{hōsh}, \textquotedblleft{}the senses, awareness\textquotedblright{}, the word inside \textbf{\ur{ہوشیار}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{be hosh}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{be hosh}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{voh ādmī be hosh thā.} — That man was unconscious.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to be grazed, then the Urdu for a scratch, then say \emph{be hosh} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{بے} \ur{ہوش} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Unconscious\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{لہولہان} (lahūluhān)}{لہولہان (lahūluhān)}]{\ur{لہولہان} (lahūluhān) — covered in blood}

\label{lesson:UR-C286-lahuluhan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a scratch, then the Urdu for unconscious.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{لہولہان}}
\textbf{\ur{لہولہان}} — \emph{lahūluhān} — \textquotedblleft{}covered in blood\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اس} \ur{کا} \ur{چہرہ} \ur{لہولہان} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{us kā chehrā lahūluhān thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
His face was covered in blood.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{لہولہان}} (\emph{lahūluhān}) is \emph{lahū}, blood, which CDIAL lists for Hindi under Sanskrit \emph{l\'{\={o}}hita}, \textquotedblleft{}red\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 11165), followed by an expressive echo, \emph{-luhān}, that makes the picture stronger.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{علاج} (ilāj)}{علاج (ilāj)}]{\ur{علاج} (ilāj) — medical treatment}

\label{lesson:UR-C286-ilaj}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for unconscious, then the Urdu for covered in blood.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{علاج}}
\textbf{\ur{علاج}} — \emph{ilāj} — \textquotedblleft{}medical treatment\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ہسپتال} \ur{میں} \ur{اس} \ur{کا} \ur{علاج} \ur{ہوا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{haspatāl meṅ us kā ilāj huā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He was treated in hospital.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{علاج}} (\emph{ilāj}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ʿilāj}, \textquotedblleft{}a remedy, a cure\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\ur{علاج} \ur{ہوا}} says that someone was treated.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for unconscious, then the Urdu for covered in blood, then say \emph{ilāj} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{کچلنا} (kuchalnā)}{کچلنا (kuchalnā)}]{\ur{کچلنا} (kuchalnā) — to crush; to run over}

\label{lesson:UR-C286-kuchalna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for covered in blood, then the Urdu for medical treatment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{کچلنا}}
\textbf{\ur{کچلنا}} — \emph{kuchalnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to crush; to run over\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ٹرک} \ur{نے} \ur{سائیکل} \ur{کو} \ur{کچل} \ur{دیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ṭrak ne sāikil ko kuchal diyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The lorry ran over the bicycle.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{پھول} \ur{کچلا}, \emph{us ne phūl kuchlā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{کچلنا}} (\emph{kuchalnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{kucalnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to trample on\textquotedblright{}, under a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 3221). \textbf{\ur{کچل} \ur{دیا}} crushes it flat, done once and for all.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kuchalnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kuchalnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭrak ne sāikil ko kuchal diyā.} — The lorry ran over the bicycle.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for covered in blood, then the Urdu for medical treatment, then say \emph{kuchalnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{کچلنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To crush; to run over\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سنبھلنا} (sambhalnā)}{سنبھلنا (sambhalnā)}]{\ur{سنبھلنا} (sambhalnā) — to steady oneself; to recover}

\label{lesson:UR-C286-sambhalna-oneself}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for medical treatment, then the Urdu for to crush.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سنبھلنا}}
\textbf{\ur{سنبھلنا}} — \emph{sambhalnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to steady oneself; to recover\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ایک} \ur{ہفتے} \ur{بعد} \ur{وہ} \ur{سنبھل} \ur{گیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ek hafte bād voh sambhal gayā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A week later he had recovered.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \ur{وہ} \ur{سنبھل} \ur{گیا}, \emph{voh sambhal gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{sā̃bhalnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be supported\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{sáṃbharati} (CDIAL 12961). It is the partner of \textbf{\ur{سنبھالنا}}: you \textbf{\ur{سنبھالنا}} something, and you \textbf{\ur{سنبھلنا}} yourself.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sambhalnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sambhalnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ek hafte bād voh sambhal gayā.} — A week later he had recovered.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for medical treatment, then the Urdu for to crush, then say \emph{sambhalnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{سنبھلنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To steady oneself; to recover\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
